newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Tokyo hit by profit-taking as Asia markets stall.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo hit by profit-taking as Asia markets stall.

text.p: Asian markets fell almost across the board on Wednesday as profit-taking after recent gains took its toll on prices.
The key Tokyo market saw 0.72 percent wiped off its value, while Hong Kong fared slightly better and shed 0.24 percent.
Sentiment in the region was seen as cautious as players awaited further leads from Wall Street and indications on the likely direction of U.S. interest rates.

Tokyo stocks were dealt a setback as profit-taking emerged to send the key Nikkei average down after big gains over the last two trading days. But brokers said that the index was likely to be supported at around 21,000, where investors' buying is said to be positioned.
The Nikkei 225 average closed down 153.84 points or 0.72 percent at 21,156.75. Its December futures shed 140 points to finish at 21,200.
"Since the average had shot up for a couple of days, activity slowed today," said a broker at a second-tier Japanese securities house.

Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index closed modestly easier, off lows but just below the important resistance level of 11,600, as profit-takers and bulls struggled to dictate the market's direction, brokers said.
"All eyes are watching the Wall Street Dow and interest rate decisions in the U.S.," said Anthony Mak, sales director at Vickers Ballas.
The Hang Seng Index closed down 27.58 points at 11,594.03 after trending as much as 95 points down during the day.
The Australian share market slipped in late trade, hit by continuing fragile metal prices and weaker industrial shares. The All Ordinaries index ended 19.30 points lower at 2235.10.
Kuala Lumpur's blue-chip Composite Index slipped 6.14 points to close at 1,128.74, while the Second Board Index closed up 4.45 points at 599.16
Thai stocks fell for the second day in a row as trade remained thin while investors watched a censure debate against the prime minister, brokers said.
The SET index moved in negative territory throughout the day to end down 12.32 points at 1,038.03.
Seoul's composite stock index rose 0.35 points to provisionally end at 782.11. But the small-cap sub-index gained 14.50 points to 1,972.79.
Taiwan was also a gainer as the weighted index closed 20.58 points, or 0.32 percent higher, at 6,499.02.
Profit-taking took Manila shares lower and the main index dropped by 11.13 points, or 0.34 percent, to 3,248.59.
Singapore shares closed lower as a short spurt of programme buying eased, with the key Straits Times Index closing down 6.74 points at 2,182.31.
In Jakarta, the Composite Index fell 2.25 points, or 0.40 percent, to close at 559.70 points.
Bombay shares finished higher on fund purchases in index-linked stocks and on a technical correction.
The 30-share index Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) index closed up 71.89 points at a provisional 3,419.26.

Hong Kong gold bullion ended at US$382.70/383.20 an ounce, unchanged from its New York close on Tuesday. A broker said trading was slow as players awaited an International Monetary Fund (IMF) meeting to discuss gold sales plans.
Asian crude prices rallied as futures firmed in the wake of U.S. stock data. On Simex (The Singapore International Monetary Exchange), November Brent crude rose 39 cents to $22.10.
At 1045 GMT, the dollar was trading at 110.16/21 yen and 1.5135/40 marks, against 110.24/31 and 1.5139/44 at Tuesday's New York close.
